t.E621.agn: In 2017 EFSA set a group acceptable daily intake (ADI) for glutamates (E620–E625) of 30 mg/kg body weight, expressed as glutamic acid, and stated that this value may be exceeded in some high-consumption scenarios. Headaches have been reported in sensitive individuals.
t.E621.body: Glutamate is absorbed from the intestine, and most of it is broken down (metabolised) in the intestinal wall before it reaches the blood.
t.E621.eff.0.t: Headaches have been reported; a causal link has not been established
t.E621.eff.1.t: The daily limit may be exceeded in some high-consumption scenarios
t.E621.eval: Glutamates (E620-E625): in 2017 EFSA set a group ADI (30 mg/kg body weight/day) and stated that this value may be exceeded in some high-consumption scenarios. The “neurotoxin” claim is not classified as such by official bodies; headaches have been reported in sensitive individuals.
t.E621.prod: Glutamic acid is produced by bacterial fermentation; its salts are obtained by neutralisation.
t.E621.summary: The sodium salt of glutamic acid (MSG). Enhances umami (savoury, meaty) taste; used in instant soups, crisps, seasonings and ready meals.
t.E621.what: Enhances the taste of food, especially umami (savoury, meaty) taste. Glutamate is an amino acid that also occurs naturally in tomatoes, cheese and meat stock.
